name: session-create-login-unacknowledged-409

graded_by.test: core/internal/httpapi/sessions_test.go — TestALoginThatWouldBeRecordedIsRefused409UntilAcknowledged: with recording enabled and login_input on, a create with a login that does not set recording_acknowledged is 409 login_recording_not_acknowledged, no connect reaches a worker and nothing is recorded; the same request with it true is 201; and with the knob off the request is accepted either way

description: A login that would be recorded needs the request's explicit consent. While the deployment's effective value is true (recording.enabled and recording.login_input both on, as GET /auth/me says), a create whose login does not set recording_acknowledged true is refused 409 login_recording_not_acknowledged: the core sends nothing to a worker, opens no connection and records nothing, and the answer echoes no field of the login. The surface re-reads /auth/me, warns the operator that the login will be recorded and repeats the request with recording_acknowledged true, which is accepted. With the knob off, or recording disabled, the same request is accepted with or without the field. The fixture grades the refusal, so it needs a deployment with the knob on, which a live run does not control (the contract's own served app has it off unless a test turns it on): it is graded by the core's own test, as the not-ssh refusal is.

error.message: the login would be recorded; acknowledge the recording and repeat the request
